internal_section_headings_verification: Verified against /tmp/calleja-fulltext.txt lines 5162-5849. Manifest seed listed 'Macro Phase: Goals and Rewards' + 'Goals' + '(further subsections — Caillois paidia/ludus; Salen+Zimmerman; Juul on magic circle)'. Full structure confirms EIGHT named subsections: 'Macro Phase: Goals and Rewards' (line 5163, opening Caillois paidia/ludus material), 'Goals' (line 5277), 'The Structure of Goals' (line 5411), 'Micro Phase: Plans, Goals, and Rewards during Gameplay' (line 5501), 'Plans and Goals' (line 5517), 'Strategies, Tactics, and Microtactics' (line 5558), 'Rewards' (line 5640), 'Ludic Involvement Summary' (line 5832). This is the MOST STRUCTURALLY ELABORATED dimension chapter in the volume — eight named subsections in 20 pages, including a closing summary subsection that is unique to Ch.9 among the six dimension chapters (none of Ch.4-8 carry a 'Summary' subsection). CRITICAL FINDING: The MANIFEST SEED 'magic circle (Huizinga via Salen+Zimmerman via Juul)' is NOT supported by the actual chapter text — Calleja does NOT engage Huizinga's magic circle in Ch.9, does NOT cite Huizinga by name in this chapter, and does NOT take up Juul's magic-circle critique here. Juul (2005) is cited but only at line 5206 (rule systems / systemic nature of games) and at line 5291 (skill-modulation). Magic circle as a thematic operates in earlier chapters (likely Ch.1 / Ch.2). Phase 2 should flag this manifest-seed misalignment.

expected_concepts: Rules / rule system (machine behind the representational surface; assigns values to objects, events, entities)
Goals (game-set / system-determined; self-set / player-determined; community-negotiated)

Paidia (Caillois 1962) — 'diversion, turbulence, free improvisation, and carefree gaiety'; ideal of uncultured / pre-linguistic play

Strategy (plans in pursuit of primary goals) — Calleja's own term-of-art
Tactics (plans in pursuit of subgoals) — Calleja's own term-of-art

expected_burke_pentad_candidate: Purpose + Act (Calleja's ludic dimension paradigmatically maps to the Purpose-Act ratio: goals are the player's purposes that organize sequences of acts; the chapter's strategy/tactics/microtactics hierarchy IS a pentadic analysis of how purposes structure acts at descending temporal scales) — anticipatory projection per plan §4.1 (provenance: anticipatory-projection). Burke's pentadic Purpose term (the 'for what / toward what end' of action) is the cleanest pentad fit for Calleja's goal-centric framing of ludic involvement, with Act (the 'what done' under the purpose's organization) as the co-anchor. The primary-goal / subgoal / microtactic hierarchy maps directly onto distal-purpose / proximal-purpose / immediate-act decomposition. Calleja's repeated framing of goals as the EXPERIENTIAL manifestation of the rule system (line 5259-5263: 'rules are not often the focus of conscious attention. Rather, the rule system manifests itself experientially in the form of decision making and the pursuit of personal and game-defined goals') matches Burke's claim that pentadic Purpose is what gives Act its motive-intelligibility. Burke is wholly absent from Calleja's text and references (cite_check: 0 hits). The Purpose+Act ratio is the volume's premier Burke-pentad-mapping site after Kinesthetic-Agency.
expected_uexkull_anchor_candidate: Wirkmal (effect-marker / effector-sign) + goal-structure (anticipatory) — per plan §3D.i. Uexküll's Funktionskreis (function-circle) decomposes the perception-action loop into Merkmal (perception-marker) and Wirkmal (effect-marker / effector-sign). Calleja's ludic-involvement micro-phase is paradigmatically Wirkmal-organized: actions are not raw motor-execution but rule-validated effector-signs that carry game-system meaning (the capture-the-flag flag at lines 5237-5256 is THE volume-defining Wirkmal exhibit — physical-screen-pixel-of-flag becomes effector-sign-of-ludic-objective via rule-system mediation). The goal-structure analysis additionally maps onto Uexküll's notion that the animal's Umwelt is organized by its biological purposes (Tonkreise): the player's game-Umwelt is organized by primary-goal / subgoal / microtactic decomposition. The Sid Meier 'set of interesting choices' aphorism aligns with Uexküll's claim that the animal's Umwelt presents itself as a structured field of action-possibilities, not as a neutral perceptual flux. Calleja has zero Uexküll vocabulary and zero biosemiotic citation. Plan §3D.i flagged the goal-structure / Wirkmal mapping as anticipatory; this chapter validates that flag.
expected_ontological_grounding_candidate: Phronesis (practical wisdom / Nicomachean Ethics VI) + deliberative phantasia (De Anima III.10-11) via Papachristou — anticipatory projection per plan §1.4 (provenance: anticipatory-projection). Papachristou's reading of Aristotelian phronesis as embodied-deliberative-capacity-applied-to-particulars, mediated by phantasia (deliberative-imagination of action-possibilities), is the cleanest ontological grounding for Calleja's micro-phase strategy/tactics/microtactics hierarchy. The fencing case study (lines 5569-5594) and the FIFA 09 case study (lines 5603-5639) are paradigmatic phronesis-exhibits: agent-confronted-with-particular-situation-deliberates-among-action-possibilities-and-acts. The microtactic concept ('decisions to immediately perform certain actions instead of others', line 5600-5602) is structurally identical to Aristotelian prohairesis (deliberative choice). Calleja's 'iterative process of planning, execution, feedback, and replanning' (line 5519-5526) is a moment-by-moment exercise of practical reasoning. Calleja has zero Aristotle hits per Phase 0 cite-check; the phronesis-grounding is wholly anticipatory. This chapter is the volume's PREMIER phronesis-anchor site (kinesthetic / spatial / shared / narrative / affective chapters do not foreground deliberation-among-particulars as Ch.9 does).
